shlokas.sanskrit: तथोक्ते तानृषीन्रामः प्रत्युवाच कृताञ्जलिः । किमाहारः किमाचारो लवणः क्व च वर्तते ।। 7.62.1 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tathokte tānṛṣīnrāmaḥ pratyuvāca kṛtāñjaliḥ | kimāhāraḥ kimācāro lavaṇaḥ kva ca vartate || 7.62.1 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: When this had been spoken, Rama, with palms joined together, replied to those sages: What is Lavana's food, what is his conduct, and where does he dwell?

shlokas.sanskrit: राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा ऋषयः सर्व एव ते । ततो निवेदयामासुर्लवणो ववृधे यथा ।। 7.62.2 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā ṛṣayaḥ sarva eva te | tato nivedayāmāsurlavaṇo vavṛdhe yathā || 7.62.2 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having heard Raghava's words, all those sages then related how Lavana had grown to such power.

shlokas.sanskrit: आहारः सर्वसत्त्वानि विशेषेण च तापसाः । आचारो रौद्रता नित्यं वासो मधुवने तथा ।। 7.62.3 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: āhāraḥ sarvasattvāni viśeṣeṇa ca tāpasāḥ | ācāro raudratā nityaṃ vāso madhuvane tathā || 7.62.3 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: His food is all living creatures, and the ascetics in particular; his conduct is one of constant ferocity, and his dwelling is in the Madhu forest.

shlokas.sanskrit: हत्वा बहुसहस्राणि सिंहव्याघ्रमृगद्विपान् । मानुषांश्चैव कुरुते नित्यमाहारमाह्निकम् ।। 7.62.4 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: hatvā bahusahasrāṇi siṃhavyāghramṛgadvipān | mānuṣāṃścaiva kurute nityamāhāramāhnikam || 7.62.4 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having slain many thousands of lions, tigers, deer, and elephants, and men as well, he makes of them his food day by day.

shlokas.sanskrit: ततो ऽन्तराणि सत्त्वानि खादते स महाबलः । संहारे समनुप्राप्ते व्यादितास्य इवान्तकः ।। 7.62.5 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tato 'ntarāṇi sattvāni khādate sa mahābalaḥ | saṃhāre samanuprāpte vyāditāsya ivāntakaḥ || 7.62.5 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then that one of great strength devours yet other creatures besides, like Death with gaping mouth when the time of dissolution has come.

shlokas.sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा राघवो वाक्यमुवाच स महामुनीन् । घातयिष्यामि तद्रक्षो ह्यपगच्छतु वो भयम् ।। 7.62.6 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tacchrutvā rāghavo vākyamuvāca sa mahāmunīn | ghātayiṣyāmi tadrakṣo hyapagacchatu vo bhayam || 7.62.6 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Hearing this, Raghava spoke these words to the great sages: I shall have that demon slain; let your fear depart.

shlokas.sanskrit: प्रतिज्ञाय तथा तेषां मुनीनामुग्रतेजसाम् । स भ्रातऽन्सहितान्सर्वानुवाच रघुनन्दनः ।। 7.62.7 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: pratijñāya tathā teṣāṃ munīnāmugratejasām | sa bhrāta'nsahitānsarvānuvāca raghunandanaḥ || 7.62.7 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having thus given his promise to those sages of fierce splendor, Raghunandana then addressed all his brothers assembled together.

shlokas.sanskrit: को हन्ता लवणं वीरः कस्यांशः स विधीयताम् । भरतस्य महाबाहोः शत्रुघ्नस्य च धीमतः ।। 7.62.8 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ko hantā lavaṇaṃ vīraḥ kasyāṃśaḥ sa vidhīyatām | bharatasya mahābāhoḥ śatrughnasya ca dhīmataḥ || 7.62.8 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Which hero shall be the slayer of Lavana? Let that task be assigned as the portion of one of them — of mighty-armed Bharata or of wise Shatrughna.

shlokas.sanskrit: राघवेणैवमुक्तस्तु भरतो वाक्यमब्रवीत् । अहमेनं वधिष्यामि ममांशः स विधीयताम् ।। 7.62.9 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: rāghaveṇaivamuktastu bharato vākyamabravīt | ahamenaṃ vadhiṣyāmi mamāṃśaḥ sa vidhīyatām || 7.62.9 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thus addressed by Raghava, Bharata spoke these words: I shall slay him; let that be assigned as my portion.

shlokas.sanskrit: भरतस्य वचः श्रुत्वा धैर्यशौर्यसमन्वितम् । लक्ष्मणावरजस्तस्थौ हित्वा सौवर्णमासनम् ।। 7.62.10 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: bharatasya vacaḥ śrutvā dhairyaśauryasamanvitam | lakṣmaṇāvarajastasthau hitvā sauvarṇamāsanam || 7.62.10 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Hearing Bharata's words, full of firmness and valor, the younger brother of Lakshmana rose, leaving his golden seat.

shlokas.sanskrit: शत्रुघ्नस्त्वब्रवीद्वाक्यं प्रणिपत्य नराधिपम् । कृतकर्मा महाबाहुर्मध्यमो रघुनन्दनः ।। 7.62.11 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: śatrughnastvabravīdvākyaṃ praṇipatya narādhipam | kṛtakarmā mahābāhurmadhyamo raghunandanaḥ || 7.62.11 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then Shatrughna, the mighty-armed delight of the Raghus, the middle one in age, whose task was accomplished, bowed before the king and spoke these words.

shlokas.sanskrit: आर्येण हि पुरा शून्या त्वयोध्या परिपालिता । सन्तापं हृदये कृत्वा आर्यस्यागमनं प्रति ।। 7.62.12 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: āryeṇa hi purā śūnyā tvayodhyā paripālitā | santāpaṃ hṛdaye kṛtvā āryasyāgamanaṃ prati || 7.62.12 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "For in former days, O noble one, the empty Ayodhya was guarded by the noble Bharata, who bore grief in his heart awaiting the return of his noble elder brother."

shlokas.sanskrit: दुःखानि च बहूनीह ह्यनुभूतानि पार्थिव । शयानो दुःखशय्यासु नन्दिग्रामे ऽवसत्पुरा ।। 7.62.13 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: duḥkhāni ca bahūnīha hyanubhūtāni pārthiva | śayāno duḥkhaśayyāsu nandigrāme 'vasatpurā || 7.62.13 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Many sorrows were endured here, O king; lying upon beds of grief, he dwelt formerly at Nandigrama."

shlokas.sanskrit: फलमूलाशनो भूत्वा जटी चीरधरस्तथा । अनुभूयेदृशं दुःखमेष राघवनन्दनः । प्रेष्ये मयि स्थिते राजन्न भूयः क्लेशमाप्नुयात् ।। 7.62.14 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: phalamūlāśano bhūtvā jaṭī cīradharastathā | anubhūyedṛśaṃ duḥkhameṣa rāghavanandanaḥ | preṣye mayi sthite rājanna bhūyaḥ kleśamāpnuyāt || 7.62.14 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Living on fruits and roots, wearing matted locks and bark garments, this delight of the Raghus endured such suffering. O king, while I, your servant, am at hand, let him not undergo affliction once again."

shlokas.sanskrit: तथा ब्रुवति शत्रुघ्ने राघवः पुनरब्रवीत् । एवं भवतु काकुत्स्थ क्रियतां मम शासनम् ।। 7.62.15 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tathā bruvati śatrughne rāghavaḥ punarabravīt | evaṃ bhavatu kākutstha kriyatāṃ mama śāsanam || 7.62.15 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: When Shatrughna had spoken thus, Raghava replied once more: "So be it, O scion of Kakutstha; let my command be carried out."

shlokas.sanskrit: राज्ये त्वामभिषेक्ष्यामि मधोस्तु नगरे शुभे । निवेशय महाबाहो भरतं यद्यवेक्षसे ।। 7.62.16 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: rājye tvāmabhiṣekṣyāmi madhostu nagare śubhe | niveśaya mahābāho bharataṃ yadyavekṣase || 7.62.16 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "I shall consecrate you to the kingdom in the auspicious city of Madhu. Settle Bharata there, O mighty-armed one, if you so regard it."

shlokas.sanskrit: शूरस्त्वं कृतविद्यश्च समर्थश्च निवेशने ।। 7.62.17 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: śūrastvaṃ kṛtavidyaśca samarthaśca niveśane || 7.62.17 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "You are valiant, accomplished in learning, and capable of founding a settlement."

shlokas.sanskrit: यो हि शत्रुं समुत्पाट्य पार्थिवस्य पुनः क्षये । न विधत्ते नृपं तत्र नरकं स हि गच्छति ।। 7.62.18 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: yo hi śatruṃ samutpāṭya pārthivasya punaḥ kṣaye | na vidhatte nṛpaṃ tatra narakaṃ sa hi gacchati || 7.62.18 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "For he who, having uprooted an enemy, does not, upon the fall of that king's realm, install a ruler there, surely goes to hell."

shlokas.sanskrit: स त्वं हत्वा मधुसुतं लवणं पापनिश्चयम् । राज्यं प्रशाधि धर्मेण वाक्यं मे यद्यवेक्षसे ।। 7.62.19 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sa tvaṃ hatvā madhusutaṃ lavaṇaṃ pāpaniścayam | rājyaṃ praśādhi dharmeṇa vākyaṃ me yadyavekṣase || 7.62.19 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Therefore, having slain Lavana, the son of Madhu, whose resolve was wicked, govern the kingdom in accordance with dharma, if you regard my word."

shlokas.sanskrit: उत्तरं च न वक्तव्यं शूर वाक्यान्तरे मम । बालेन पूर्वजस्याज्ञा कर्तव्या नात्र संशयः ।। 7.62.20 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: uttaraṃ ca na vaktavyaṃ śūra vākyāntare mama | bālena pūrvajasyājñā kartavyā nātra saṃśayaḥ || 7.62.20 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "And no reply is to be made, O hero, in answer to my words. By a younger one the command of an elder must be carried out; in this there is no doubt."

shlokas.sanskrit: अभिषेकं च काकुत्स्थ प्रतीच्छस्व मयोद्यतम् । वसिष्ठप्रमुखैर्विप्रैर्विधिमन्त्रपुरस्कृतम् ।। 7.62.21 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: abhiṣekaṃ ca kākutstha pratīcchasva mayodyatam | vasiṣṭhapramukhairviprairvidhimantrapuraskṛtam || 7.62.21 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "And accept, O scion of Kakutstha, the consecration prepared by me, attended by the brahmins led by Vasishtha and furnished with the prescribed rites and sacred mantras."

shlokas.sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे द्विषष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 62।।
shlokas.transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmaduttarakāṇḍe dviṣaṣṭitamaḥ sargaḥ || 62||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thus, in the sacred and glorious Ramayana, the first poem composed by Valmiki, in the venerable Uttara Kanda, ends the sixty-second canto.
